verdict_reason: Reproduced Ethayarajh 2019's RELEASED gpt2 numbers. Running BLME's _intra_sentence_mean_cosine and _baseline_anisotropy on gpt2 over the repo's own sts.csv gives a 13-layer IntraSim profile matching kawine/contextual's published gpt2/embedding_space_stats.json to mean absolute difference 0.0110 (max 0.030, Pearson 0.9949) and the anisotropy profile to mean 0.0176, including the distinctive layer-12 spike 0.9868 vs published 0.990. The MEV kernel equals sklearn PCA(1).explained_variance_ratio_[0] to the last bit (0.553649425680387 both) and the TruncatedSVD twin to 3.1e-14, and the released variance_explained.csv over 6875 words averages 0.3054 on layers 2-11, confirming the centred convention the code uses.
comparable_reason: The anisotropy-corrected outputs are width-flat and offset-free. On isotropic Gaussian clouds at n=200 the corrected SelfSim reads +0.00232 / +0.00016 / +0.00146 / -0.00012 / -0.00017 at d = 16 / 64 / 256 / 768 / 2048; adding a common +2 offset to every coordinate drives raw SelfSim to 0.800 at every width and the corrected form still reads within +-0.0004 of zero. The RAW selfsim/intrasim twins are not comparable -- they are dominated by whatever anisotropy the model happens to have -- which is exactly why Ethayarajh Sec. 3.4 reports the adjusted numbers, and the module docstring says so.
github_reason: Fetched analyze.py, sts.csv, gpt2/embedding_space_stats.json and gpt2/variance_explained.csv from the released repo. Confirmed BLME's IntraSim is the reference's 'mean cosine similarity between sentence and words' (sentence vector = mean of token vectors, then mean cosine of each token to it) and _baseline_anisotropy is its 'mean cosine similarity across words' (one random token per sentence, random pairs), and reproduced both published per-layer profiles on gpt2. Confirmed the MEV convention is sklearn PCA (centred), matching variance_explained_by_pc.
paper_reason: kawine/contextual gpt2/embedding_space_stats.json, IntraSim per layer 0..12 published as 0.808 / 0.825 / 0.583 / 0.549 / 0.537 / 0.559 / 0.586 / 0.614 / 0.635 / 0.658 / 0.693 / 0.768 / 0.990; BLME gives 0.8129 / 0.8134 / 0.5527 / 0.5319 / 0.5368 / 0.5736 / 0.5985 / 0.6260 / 0.6456 / 0.6628 / 0.6837 / 0.7563 / 0.9868 -- mean |diff| 0.0110, worst 0.030 (layer 2), relative error 1.9% on the mean. The anisotropy row matches to mean 0.0176. Residual is corpus size (198 released sentences vs their 1000-sample estimate), not method. Separately, the released variance_explained.csv gives mean raw MEV 0.3054 over layers 2-11, reproducing the paper's own '~30%' statement and confirming the centred-PCA convention.
confounds_reason: Corrected SelfSim is within +-0.0023 of zero on an isotropic null at every width d = 16..2048 (no trend), and removes a synthetic 0.800 common-offset anisotropy to within 0.0004 at all five widths. Cosines are dimensionless and vocabulary does not enter. The raw twins do carry the model's anisotropy, which is architecture-dependent -- but that is the quantity Ethayarajh defines, and the corrected pair is the reported one.
defects: CODE, UNREACHABLE AND SHARED WITH THE REFERENCE: _cosine_pairwise_mean (contextualization.py:50-53) is the ONE helper in this file still on the raw np.linalg.norm; its sibling _intra_sentence_mean_cosine and _baseline_anisotropy both use safe_unit_rows. On a scale ladder it returns exactly 0.000000000000 at 1e-30, 1e-25 and 1e25 where the true SelfSim is 0.548553507, while IntraSim on the identical data is stable to 7e-9. I do NOT make this verdict-driving: the released reference kernel, scipy.spatial.distance.cosine on float32, returns nan at exactly those same scales (measured), and the failure needs a row norm below ~4e-23 or above ~1.8e19 while gpt2's real token-vector norms span 4.5739 to 3156.2879 -- a 5.9e15x headroom. Returning 0.0 rather than NaN is nonetheless a false zero: 0.0 is a legal SelfSim value.

COMPARABILITY (not implementation): the raw selfsim/intrasim outputs are dominated by model anisotropy -- a synthetic common +2 offset alone produces raw SelfSim 0.800 at every width. Use only the *_corrected family for cross-model comparison, as the paper does.

CONFIG (not implementation): defaults.yaml ships num_samples: 1000 for this task; a study config that lowers it shrinks both the SelfSim pair pool and the 2000-pair anisotropy baseline, and the baseline is subtracted from every reported statistic.
